newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey tense ahead of key military meeting.
newsitem.headline: Turkey tense ahead of key military meeting.

text.p: Turkey's Islamist-led government, fresh from a censure motion win, prepared on Wednesday for a crucial meeting later this week with the restive chiefs of the secularist armed forces.

But main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz, quick to pronounce the government dead despite the failure of the motion against it, called for a broad based coalition without the Islamist Welfare Party to dispel the danger of any coup by the military.

Tension is expected to be high at Friday's meeting of the National Security Council (NSC), attended by Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, because of recent public squabbling between the generals and the Islamist wing of the coalition.
The armed forces have warned the coalition of Erbakan's Islamists and the pro-Western True Path Party times in recent weeks against increasing the role of Islam in public life.
"The tension, or the events that have caused tension, will be discussed at the NSC," the Hurriyet daily quoted Erbakan aide Aydin Menderes as saying.
Yilmaz denied he was scare-mongering by speculating that the tensions could lead to a fourth military coup since 1960.
"I say the regime in this country is in danger, but I am actually calling for a united front against any possible coup," he told his MPs in parliament.
Yilmaz's Motherland Party has presented parliament with another censure motion -- expected to be discussed next week -- over unequal pay rises for civil servants.

Erbakan, whose party won a narrow plurality of 21 percent in general elections in December, 1995, survived a challenge to his rule this week when MPs voted 281 to 246 to reject two leftist bids to hold a ballot on bringing down the coalition for allegedly threatening the country's secular system.
Welfare's Menderes predicted, however, that Erbakan would assure the military on Friday that he was not bent on turning NATO member Turkey into a strict Islamic state.
